\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  An invertible sheaf is given on a finite affine cover by finitely many finitely presented
  rank-one modules, transition isomorphisms, and finitely many cocycle equations.  All this
  data, as well as an isomorphism between two such data, descends to a finite stage of a
  filtered union.  The degree-zero condition is preserved and reflected after field extension
  because degree is invariant under scalar extension.  This proves filtered compatibility.
  Faithfully flat descent for finitely presented modules descends the local line bundles and
  their transition maps, while the cocycle equation gives effectivity and uniqueness.  Passing
  to the quotient by line bundles from the base and then to the etale sheafification preserves
  this descent statement, since both equivalence and effectivity may be checked after a common
  faithfully flat refinement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A finite Galois stage for the Picard representer]
  \label{thm:pic0FiniteGaloisStage}
  \uses{def:pic0SepClosedDescentInput, thm:pic0SepClosedDescentInput_exists,
    thm:pic0DescentCompatibility}
  \notready
  Let \(k^s\) be a separable closure of \(k\).  The separably closed descent package descends
  to a finite Galois extension \(L/k\): there are a finite-type proper group scheme \(J_L\)
  representing \(\mathrm{pic}^0(C_L)\), its universal class, and a semilinear action of
  \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)\) preserving that class and satisfying the cocycle condition.
  Every orbit of this action is contained in an affine open of \(J_L\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  Because \(J_{k^s}\) is of finite presentation, it descends to a finite subextension
  \(L_0/k\).  The universal class descends after enlarging \(L_0\), by
  Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0DescentCompatibility}.  The natural transformation defined by the
  descended class becomes the given representation after extension to \(k^s\); faithful flat
  descent for both the Yoneda functor and the Picard sheaf shows that it is already an
  isomorphism over \(L_0\).  Properness, the group operations, and their finitely many axioms
  also descend after one further finite extension.  Enlarge \(L_0\) to a finite Galois
  extension \(L/k\).

  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)\), both \(\sigma^*J_L\) and \(J_L\), equipped with
  their transported universal classes, represent the same functor.  Yoneda uniqueness gives
  a unique semilinear isomorphism between them.  The two composites associated to
  \(\sigma\tau\) carry the universal class to the same element, so uniqueness proves the
  cocycle equation.  A proper finite-type group scheme over a field is projective.  Given a
  finite Galois orbit, choose a closed specialization of each of its finitely many points.
  For a sufficiently high power of an ample line bundle, restriction of global sections to
  the resulting finite closed subscheme is surjective.  Lift the section that is \(1\) at
  every member of that subscheme.  Its nonvanishing locus contains the chosen closed
  specializations and therefore the original orbit; as the complement of an ample effective
  divisor, this locus is affine.  This proves the final certificate.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Stable affine neighbourhoods for a finite action]
  \label{lem:finiteGalois_stableAffineCover}
  \notready
  Let a finite group \(G\) act on a separated scheme \(X\).  If every \(G\)-orbit is contained
  in an affine open, then \(X\) has a \(G\)-stable affine open cover.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
  Fix \(x\in X\) and choose an affine open \(V\) containing its whole orbit.  Every translate
  \(gV\) also contains that orbit.  Hence
  \(U_x=\bigcap_{g\in G}gV\) is a \(G\)-stable open containing \(x\).  A finite intersection
  of affine opens in a separated scheme is affine: the intersection of two is the inverse
  image of the affine \(V\times V'\) under the affine diagonal, and induction handles the
  finite intersection.  The opens \(U_x\), as \(x\) varies, form the required cover.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite Galois descent of a scheme]
  \label{thm:finiteGalois_schemeDescent}
  \uses{lem:finiteGalois_stableAffineCover}
  \notready
  Let \(L/k\) be finite Galois and let an \(L\)-scheme \(X_L\) carry a semilinear Galois
  action satisfying the cocycle condition.  If every orbit lies in an affine open, then there
  are a \(k\)-scheme \(X\) and an isomorphism
  \(X\times_kL\simeq X_L\) inducing the given action.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  By Lemma~\ref{lem:finiteGalois_stableAffineCover}, cover \(X_L\) by stable affine opens
  \(U_i=\Spec A_i\).  Semilinear Galois descent for algebras gives
  \(B_i=A_i^G\) and an isomorphism \(L\otimes_kB_i\simeq A_i\).  Since \(X_L\) is separated,
  every overlap \(U_i\cap U_j\) and every triple overlap is affine and stable.  Applying the
  same invariant construction to these overlaps descends both open immersions
  \(U_i\cap U_j\rightrightarrows U_i,U_j\); faithful flatness of \(L/k\) reflects the open
  immersions and their cocycle identities.  The affine schemes \(\Spec B_i\) therefore glue
  along the descended overlaps to a \(k\)-scheme \(X\).  The local isomorphisms
  \(L\otimes_kB_i\simeq A_i\) agree on overlaps and glue to
  \(X\times_kL\simeq X_L\).  Their defining invariant maps identify the canonical descent
  action with the prescribed semilinear action.

    26	That packaging had never been written.  `PicRepDatum` occurs in no other Lean file in the
    27	tree: the defeq is recorded as an `example`, so nothing *consumes* it, and DAT-J's assembly
    28	was left as the pair (DAT-G output, qc) with no term joining them.  This file writes it.

    30	The content is exactly the interface, so it is short by design — but it is not nothing:
    31	writing it is what turns "DAT-G produces a datum over `k'`, and separately DAT-J wants one
    32	over `k`" into a single arrow, and it is what makes the remaining DAT-J debt *visibly* two

    26	/-- An equivariant map from the finite-Galois base change of an object over
    27	`Spec K` to a semilinearly acted `L`-scheme. -/
    28	structure GaloisEquivariantOver
    29	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    30	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    31	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    32	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) where
    33	  hom : pullback T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X
    34	  commutes : hom ≫ f =
    35	    pullback.snd T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
    36	  equivariant : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L T.hom).IsEquivariant rho hom

    49	  commutes := by
    50	    rw [Category.assoc, h.commutes, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
    51	  equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    52	    T.hom T'.hom rho h.equivariant a.left a.w

    58	  cases h'

    59	/-- Restriction of sections is strictly functorial. -/
    60	lemma resAlgHom_comp (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {U V W : T.left.Opens} (h : U ≤ V)
    61	    (h' : V ≤ W) :
    62	    (resAlgHom T h).comp (resAlgHom T h') = resAlgHom T (h.trans h') := by
    63	  have key : T.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h').op ≫ T.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op
    64	      = T.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h.trans h')).op := by
    65	    rw [← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
    66	  ext s
    67	  exact congr($(key).hom s)
    68	
    69	/-- Restriction along the trivial inclusion is the identity. -/
    70	lemma resAlgHom_rfl (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {U : T.left.Opens} (h : U ≤ U) :
    71	    resAlgHom T h = AlgHom.id k Γ(T.left, U) := by
    72	  have key : T.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op = 𝟙 Γ(T.left, U) := by
    73	    rw [show (homOfLE h).op = 𝟙 (Opposite.op U) from rfl, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]
    74	  ext s

    11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
    12	
    13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
    14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
    15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
    16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
    19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
    20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
    22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
    24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
    25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
    26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
    27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
    28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
    29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
    30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
    31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
    32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
    34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
    35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
    36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
    37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
    38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
    39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
    40	-/

   273	section field
   274	
   275	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
   276	
   277	/-- The carrier of a cover of a field (indeed, of any nontrivial base) is nontrivial. -/
   278	theorem nontrivial_carrier (E : EtaleCover A) [Nontrivial A] : Nontrivial E.Carrier :=
   279	  PrimeSpectrum.nonempty_iff_nontrivial.mp
   280	    ⟨(E.comap_surjective (Nonempty.some inferInstance)).choose⟩
   281	
   282	/-- **Field cofinality**: over a field, every presented étale cover is refined by a finite
   283	separable field extension.  This single-factor refinement is what makes field-extension
   284	covers cofinal among étale covers of `Spec K`: the étale carrier is a finite product of
   285	finite separable extensions of `K`, and projection to any one factor still covers the
   286	(one-point) spectrum of `K`. -/
   287	theorem exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom (E : EtaleCover K) :
   288	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L)
   289	      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L), Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L) := by
   290	  haveI : Nontrivial E.Carrier := E.nontrivial_carrier
   291	  obtain ⟨I, hI, Ai, hfield, halg, e, h⟩ :=
   292	    (Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod K E.Carrier).mp inferInstance
   293	  haveI : Nonempty I := by
   294	    by_contra hempty
   295	    haveI : IsEmpty I := not_nonempty_iff.mp hempty
   296	    haveI : Subsingleton E.Carrier := e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mpr inferInstance
   297	    exact false_of_nontrivial_of_subsingleton E.Carrier
   298	  obtain ⟨i⟩ := ‹Nonempty I›
   299	  exact ⟨Ai i, hfield i, halg i, (h i).1, (h i).2,
   300	    ⟨(Pi.evalAlgHom K Ai i).comp e.toAlgHom⟩⟩
   301	
   302	variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
   303	
   304	instance : Algebra.Etale K L where
   305	  formallyEtale := Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_isSeparable K L
   306	  finitePresentation :=
   307	    (Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType (R := K) (A := L)).mp inferInstance
   308	
   309	/-- A finite separable field extension as an étale cover of `Spec K` (the spectrum map
   310	between the one-point spectra is trivially surjective). -/
   311	noncomputable def ofField : EtaleCover K :=
   312	  .of L fun _ => ⟨default, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
   313	
   314	/-- The carrier of the field cover is the field extension itself. -/
   315	noncomputable def ofFieldEquiv : (ofField (K := K) L).Carrier ≃ₐ[K] L :=
   316	  ofEquiv L _
   317	
   318	end field
   319	
   320	end EtaleCover
   321	
   322	end Algebra

     9	/-!
    10	# The relative Picard functor on affine test algebras
    11	
    12	The étale sheafification of the relative Picard functor is computed over *affine* test
    13	objects, where a test object is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra `A` (the landed
    14	`AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A : Over (Spec k)`) and a test map is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
    15	map.  This file provides the algebra-indexed face of the relative Picard functor:
    16	
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.overSpecMap f`: `Spec` of a `k`-algebra map `f : A →ₐ[k] B`, as a
    18	  morphism `overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A` of `Over (Spec k)`, strictly functorial
    19	  (`overSpecMap_id`, `overSpecMap_comp`).
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap C f`: restriction of relative Picard classes along
    21	  `Spec f`, a group homomorphism `relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B)`,
    22	  covariantly functorial in the algebra (`relPicAlgMap_id`, `relPicAlgMap_comp`).
    23	
    24	The étale plus construction (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`) consumes only this interface: descent
    25	classes on an étale cover are an equalizer of two `relPicAlgMap`s, and all refinement
    26	transports are `relPicAlgMap`s of `A`-algebra maps restricted to `k`.
    27	-/

     9	# The parameterized transport core of the étale plus construction
    10	
    11	The Wave-7 plumbing shared by the curve-direction functoriality (`PicEtAff.curveMap`,
    12	`Picard/PicEtAffCurveMap.lean`) and the base-field shuffle (`PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle`,
    13	`Picard/PicEtAffBaseFieldShuffle.lean`): transporting étale-plus Picard classes along a
    14	family of scheme morphisms between the product carriers of two curve bundles — possibly
    15	over *different* base fields — indexed by the literally shared étale covers of the affine
    16	test.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.RelPicTransportFamily kT D E`: the input datum.  For curve bundles
    19	  `D` over `kD` and `E` over `kE`, a family of scheme morphisms
    20	  `hom B : (D ⊗ overSpec kD B).left ⟶ (E ⊗ overSpec kE B).left`, compatible with the
    21	  second projections (`hom_snd`) and natural against pairs of algebra maps with equal
    22	  underlying functions (`hom_naturality`).  The family is indexed by all test algebras
    23	  `B` carrying algebra structures over `kD`, `kE` and a common overfield `kT` in scalar
    24	  towers `kD → kT → B` and `kE → kT → B`; `kT` mediates between the two base fields
    25	  without relating them (`kT = kD = kE` for the curve-morphism family; `kT = L` for the
    26	  base-field shuffle, where `{kD, kE} = {k, L}`).

    28	  Picard groups, with `relPicHom_mk` and the bilateral naturality square
    29	  `relPicAlgMap_relPicHom` against restriction along same-function algebra-map pairs.
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.RelPicTransportFamily.descentHom`: descent classes map to descent
    31	  classes over the shared cover index, commuting with refinement transport
    32	  (`descentHom_descentMap`).

    34	  `PicEtAff E A →* PicEtAff D A` of étale-plus groups, with the `mk`-computation rule
    35	  (`picEtAffHom_mk`), naturality of the unit (`picEtAffHom_unit`), the bilateral
    36	  restriction squares (`map_picEtAffHom`, `mapAlg_picEtAffHom`), and the two-sided
    37	  collapse `picEtAffHom_picEtAffHom` (families with pointwise-inverse scheme morphisms
    38	  induce mutually inverse transports — the `≃*` engine of the base-field shuffle).

    40	Everything is stated through the landed `relPicMk`/`relPic.ind`/`relPicAlgMap` and
    41	`PicEtAff.mk`/`ind`/`mk_eq_mk_iff`/`descentMap` interfaces; nothing unfolds the plus

/-- A scheme `X` is Noetherian if it is locally Noetherian and compact. -/
@[mk_iff]
class IsNoetherian (X : Scheme) : Prop extends IsLocallyNoetherian X, CompactSpace X

/-- A scheme is Noetherian if and only if it is covered by finitely many affine opens whose
sections are Noetherian rings. -/
theorem isNoetherian_iff_of_finite_iSup_eq_top {ι} [Finite ι] {S : ι → X.affineOpens}
    (hS : (⨆ i, S i : X.Opens) = ⊤) :
    IsNoetherian X ↔ ∀ i, IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, S i) := by
  constructor
  · intro h i
    apply (isLocallyNoetherian_iff_of_iSup_eq_top hS).mp
    exact h.toIsLocallyNoetherian
  · intro h
    convert! IsNoetherian.mk
    · exact isLocallyNoetherian_of_affine_cover hS h
    · constructor
      rw [← Opens.coe_top, ← hS, Opens.iSup_mk]
      apply isCompact_iUnion
      intro i
      apply isCompact_iff_isCompact_univ.mpr
      convert! CompactSpace.isCompact_univ
      have : NoetherianSpace (S i) := by
        apply noetherianSpace_of_isAffineOpen (S i).1 (S i).2
      apply NoetherianSpace.compactSpace (S i)

/-- A version of `isNoetherian_iff_of_finite_iSup_eq_top` using `Scheme.OpenCover`. -/
theorem isNoetherian_iff_of_finite_affine_openCover {𝒰 : Scheme.OpenCover.{v, u} X}
    [Finite 𝒰.I₀] [∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i)] :
    IsNoetherian X ↔ ∀ (i : 𝒰.I₀), IsNoetherianRing Γ(𝒰.X i, ⊤) := by
  constructor
  · intro h i
    apply (isLocallyNoetherian_iff_of_affine_openCover _).mp
    exact h.toIsLocallyNoetherian
  · intro hNoeth
    convert! IsNoetherian.mk
    · exact (isLocallyNoetherian_iff_of_affine_openCover _).mpr hNoeth
    · exact Scheme.OpenCover.compactSpace 𝒰

/-- A Noetherian scheme has a Noetherian underlying topological space. -/
@[stacks 01OZ]
instance (priority := 100) IsNoetherian.noetherianSpace [IsNoetherian X] :
    NoetherianSpace X := by
  apply TopologicalSpace.noetherian_univ_iff.mp
  let 𝒰 := X.affineCover.finiteSubcover
  rw [← 𝒰.iUnion_range]
  suffices ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, NoetherianSpace (Set.range <| (𝒰.f i)) by
    apply NoetherianSpace.iUnion
  intro i
  have : IsAffine (𝒰.X i) := by
    rw [X.affineCover.finiteSubcover_X]
    apply Scheme.isAffine_affineCover
  let U : X.affineOpens := ⟨Scheme.Hom.opensRange (𝒰.f i), isAffineOpen_opensRange _⟩
  convert! noetherianSpace_of_isAffineOpen U.1 U.2
  apply IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian

theorem exists_fg_forall_mem_range_stageMap {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (f : ι → R ⊗[k] A) :
    ∃ S : Subalgebra k A, S.FG ∧ ∀ i, ∃ y : R ⊗[k] S, stageMap R S y = f i := by
  cases nonempty_fintype ι
  choose Sf hSf hmem using fun i => exists_fg_mem_range_stageMap R (f i)
  refine ⟨Finset.univ.sup Sf, ?_, fun i =>
    exists_stageMap_eq_of_le R (Finset.le_sup (Finset.mem_univ i)) (hmem i)⟩
  exact Finset.sup_induction Subalgebra.fg_bot (fun a ha b hb => ha.sup hb)
    fun i _ => hSf i

   127	/-! ## §1. Directed exhaustion by finitely generated subalgebras -/
   128	
   129	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   130	
   131	/-- Every element of a commutative `k`-algebra lies in a finitely generated
   132	`k`-subalgebra (namely `Algebra.adjoin k {a}`).  Together with
   133	`Subalgebra.FG.sup` (directedness) this is the exhaustion
   134	`A = ⋃ (S : Subalgebra k A) (_ : S.FG), S` underlying the whole `B2` brick. -/
   135	theorem exists_fg_mem (a : A) : ∃ S : Subalgebra k A, S.FG ∧ a ∈ S :=
   136	  ⟨Algebra.adjoin k {a}, by simpa using Subalgebra.fg_adjoin_finset {a},
   137	    Algebra.self_mem_adjoin_singleton k a⟩
   138	
   139	variable (R : Type w) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   140	
   141	/-- The **stage map** of the filtered-colimit presentation: the canonical
   142	`k`-algebra map `R ⊗[k] S → R ⊗[k] A` induced by a subalgebra `S ≤ A`.
   143	In the campaign instantiation `R` is a section ring of the standard 2-affine
   144	cover of the curve `C` and `S` runs over the finitely generated stages of the
   145	base ring `A`.  Injective because `k` is a field (`stageMap_injective`). -/
   146	def stageMap (S : Subalgebra k A) : R ⊗[k] S →ₐ[k] R ⊗[k] A :=
   147	  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id k R) S.val
   148	
   149	@[simp]
   150	lemma stageMap_tmul (S : Subalgebra k A) (r : R) (s : S) :
   151	    stageMap R S (r ⊗ₜ s) = r ⊗ₜ (s : A) :=
   152	  rfl
   153	
   154	/-- The **transition map** between two stages `S ≤ T` of the filtered-colimit
   155	presentation, `R ⊗[k] S → R ⊗[k] T`. -/
   156	def transitionMap {S T : Subalgebra k A} (h : S ≤ T) :
   157	    R ⊗[k] S →ₐ[k] R ⊗[k] T :=
   158	  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id k R) (Subalgebra.inclusion h)
   159	
   160	@[simp]
   161	lemma transitionMap_tmul {S T : Subalgebra k A} (h : S ≤ T) (r : R) (s : S) :
   162	    transitionMap R h (r ⊗ₜ s) = r ⊗ₜ Subalgebra.inclusion h s :=
   163	  rfl
   164	
   165	/-- Transition triangle: the stage maps are compatible with the transitions,
   166	`stageMap T ∘ transitionMap (S ≤ T) = stageMap S`. -/
   167	theorem stageMap_comp_transitionMap {S T : Subalgebra k A} (h : S ≤ T) :
   168	    (stageMap R T).comp (transitionMap R h) = stageMap R S := by
   169	  rw [stageMap, stageMap, transitionMap, ← Algebra.TensorProduct.map_comp]
   170	  simp
   171	
   172	/-- Pointwise transition triangle. -/
   173	theorem stageMap_transitionMap_apply {S T : Subalgebra k A} (h : S ≤ T)
   174	    (x : R ⊗[k] S) :
   175	    stageMap R T (transitionMap R h x) = stageMap R S x := by
   176	  rw [← AlgHom.comp_apply, stageMap_comp_transitionMap]
   177	
   178	/-- **Stage maps are injective.**  Because `k` is a field, `R` is a flat
   179	(indeed free) `k`-module, so tensoring the injection `S ↪ A` with `R`
   180	preserves injectivity.  This is what upgrades the filtered colimit to a
   181	directed *union*: equalities of descended elements reflect at every stage
   182	(no later-stage equalization needed), which is strictly stronger than the
   183	generic Stacks `0B8W` bookkeeping. -/
   184	theorem stageMap_injective (S : Subalgebra k A) :
   185	    Function.Injective (stageMap R S) := by
   186	  have h : (stageMap R S).toLinearMap = LinearMap.lTensor R S.val.toLinearMap :=
   187	    TensorProduct.ext' fun r s => rfl
   188	  intro x y hxy
   189	  refine Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap (M := R)
   190	    S.val.toLinearMap (fun a b hab => Subtype.ext hab) ?_
   191	  rw [← h]
   192	  exact hxy
   193	
   194	/-- **Element descent** (Stacks `0B8W`, elementary form): every element of
   195	`R ⊗[k] A` comes from `R ⊗[k] S` for some finitely generated `k`-subalgebra
   196	`S ≤ A`. -/
   197	theorem exists_fg_mem_range_stageMap (x : R ⊗[k] A) :
   198	    ∃ S : Subalgebra k A, S.FG ∧ ∃ y : R ⊗[k] S, stageMap R S y = x := by
   199	  refine TensorProduct.induction_on x ?_ ?_ ?_
   200	  · exact ⟨⊥, Subalgebra.fg_bot, 0, map_zero _⟩
   201	  · intro r a
   202	    exact ⟨Algebra.adjoin k {a}, by simpa using Subalgebra.fg_adjoin_finset {a},
   203	      r ⊗ₜ ⟨a, Algebra.self_mem_adjoin_singleton k a⟩, rfl⟩
   204	  · rintro x y ⟨S₁, hS₁, x₁, hx₁⟩ ⟨S₂, hS₂, y₂, hy₂⟩
   205	    refine ⟨S₁ ⊔ S₂, hS₁.sup hS₂,
   206	      transitionMap R (le_sup_left : S₁ ≤ S₁ ⊔ S₂) x₁
   207	        + transitionMap R (le_sup_right : S₂ ≤ S₁ ⊔ S₂) y₂, ?_⟩
   208	    rw [map_add, stageMap_transitionMap_apply, stageMap_transitionMap_apply,
   209	      hx₁, hy₂]
   210	
   211	/-- Monotonicity of the stage images: anything descended to `S` is descended
   212	to every larger stage `T ≥ S`. -/
   213	theorem exists_stageMap_eq_of_le {S T : Subalgebra k A} (h : S ≤ T)
   214	    {x : R ⊗[k] A} (hx : ∃ y : R ⊗[k] S, stageMap R S y = x) :
   215	    ∃ y : R ⊗[k] T, stageMap R T y = x := by
   216	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hx
   217	  exact ⟨transitionMap R h y, stageMap_transitionMap_apply R h y⟩
   218	
   219	/-- **Finite-family descent**: finitely many elements of `R ⊗[k] A` descend
   220	to a *common* finitely generated stage (directedness via `Finset.sup`).
   221	This is the form `G1` uses to spread a finite glueing datum to a finite
   222	level. -/
   223	theorem exists_fg_forall_mem_range_stageMap {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
   224	    (f : ι → R ⊗[k] A) :
   225	    ∃ S : Subalgebra k A, S.FG ∧ ∀ i, ∃ y : R ⊗[k] S, stageMap R S y = f i := by
   226	  cases nonempty_fintype ι
   227	  choose Sf hSf hmem using fun i => exists_fg_mem_range_stageMap R (f i)
   228	  refine ⟨Finset.univ.sup Sf, ?_, fun i =>
   229	    exists_stageMap_eq_of_le R (Finset.le_sup (Finset.mem_univ i)) (hmem i)⟩
   230	  exact Finset.sup_induction Subalgebra.fg_bot (fun a ha b hb => ha.sup hb)
   231	    fun i _ => hSf i

   233	/-- **Unit descent** (Stacks `0B8W` for `𝔾ₘ`-valued data): a unit of
   234	`R ⊗[k] A` descends, *as a unit*, to a finitely generated stage — descend the
   235	element and its inverse to a common stage and reflect the equation
   236	`x·y = 1` by injectivity of the stage map. -/
   237	theorem exists_fg_isUnit_stageMap_eq {u : R ⊗[k] A} (hu : IsUnit u) :
   238	    ∃ S : Subalgebra k A, S.FG ∧
   239	      ∃ x : R ⊗[k] S, IsUnit x ∧ stageMap R S x = u := by
   240	  obtain ⟨S, hS, hmem⟩ := exists_fg_forall_mem_range_stageMap R
   241	    ![u, ((hu.unit⁻¹ : (R ⊗[k] A)ˣ) : R ⊗[k] A)]
   242	  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hmem 0
   243	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hmem 1
   244	  simp only [Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one] at hx hy
   245	  have hxy : x * y = 1 := by
   246	    apply stageMap_injective R S
   247	    rw [map_mul, map_one, hx, hy, IsUnit.mul_val_inv]
   248	  exact ⟨S, hS, x, IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one y hxy, hx⟩
   249	
   250	/-- **Unit reflection at a larger stage**: if a stage element becomes a unit
   251	over `A`, it is already a unit at some larger finitely generated stage.
   252	(At the *same* stage this is false — the inverse need not live there — which
   253	is exactly the "descend the property, not just the element" phenomenon of
   254	filtered colimits.) -/
   255	theorem exists_fg_le_isUnit_transitionMap {S : Subalgebra k A} (hS : S.FG)
   256	    {x : R ⊗[k] S} (hx : IsUnit (stageMap R S x)) :
   257	    ∃ (T : Subalgebra k A) (hle : S ≤ T), T.FG ∧
   258	      IsUnit (transitionMap R hle x) := by
   259	  obtain ⟨S', hS', y, hy, hy'⟩ := exists_fg_isUnit_stageMap_eq R hx
   260	  refine ⟨S ⊔ S', le_sup_left, hS.sup hS', ?_⟩
   261	  have heq : transitionMap R (le_sup_left : S ≤ S ⊔ S') x
   262	      = transitionMap R (le_sup_right : S' ≤ S ⊔ S') y := by
   263	    apply stageMap_injective R (S ⊔ S')
   264	    rw [stageMap_transitionMap_apply, stageMap_transitionMap_apply, hy']
   265	  rw [heq]
   266	  exact hy.map (transitionMap R le_sup_right)

Audit conclusion: `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C` is not derivable by a bounded assembly from the landed PicEt/Pic0 APIs, and it would not by itself spread the separably closed representing scheme.

The smallest Phase-7-specific colimit target is the concrete delta theorem, not the universal residual:

```lean
theorem preservesColimit_pic0_deltaScheme
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
    PreservesColimit
      (DatG0.deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K)).op
      (pic0TypeFunctor C)
```

This is exactly the conclusion currently obtained only from the residual at [PicRepColimitMountain.lean:244](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicRepColimitMountain.lean:244). The finite-subextension diagram, its ring colimit, affine transitions, qcqs stages, and scheme limit are already complete at lines 55, 83, 113, 128, 149, 154, 159, and 195. The universal `Prop` is at [PicRepColimitCompat.lean:136](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicRepColimitCompat.lean:136); only base-change transport is proved at line 150.

The first genuine obstruction to that delta theorem is finite descent and equality reflection for `PicEtAff` representatives:

- An `EtaleCover` contains a presented algebra plus étaleness and spectrum-surjectivity at [EtaleCover.lean:64](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:64), but only forward base change exists at line 238. No theorem descends such a cover to a filtered stage.
- `PicEtAff` is a quotient of `descentClasses` at [PicEtAff.lean:76](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicEtAff.lean:76) and [PicEtAff.lean:218](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicEtAff.lean:218); equality requires a common refinement at line 235. Neither representatives nor refinement witnesses have finite-stage descent.
- `relPic` is built from `CechPic` at [RelPic.lean:52](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RelPic.lean:52). `CechPic` uses point-indexed covers and common point-indexed refinements at [Pic.lean:43](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic.lean:43), with no finite normalization or filtered descent.
- The affine comparison [PicEt.lean:235](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicEt.lean:235), Zariski sheaf machinery, and degree base-change lemmas [DegreeZeroBaseField.lean:87](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DegreeZeroBaseField.lean:87) transport already-constructed data; they do not supply this finite descent.

Separately, the first theorem that actually crosses the finite-stage boundary for the representative is an object-spreading result of the following form:

```lean
theorem exists_finSubext_baseChange_iso_of_finitePresentation
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
    (J : Over (Spec (.of K)))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation J.hom]
    [QuasiCompact J.hom]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace J.left] :
    ∃ (L : DatG0.FinSubext k K)
      (J₀ : Over (Spec (.of L.1))),
      Nonempty ((baseChange L.1 K).obj J₀ ≅ J)
```

No such essential-surjectivity theorem exists in-tree or in the pinned mathlib. The nearby limit APIs only spread maps and affine opens of an object already known as a limit: `exists_isOpenCover_and_isAffine` and `exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation` in `AffineTransitionLimit.lean` lines 1078 and 1177.

One honest bounded proof unit can close immediately:

```lean
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_pic0_sepClosed_representableBy :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation
      (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.hom :=
  LocallyOfFinitePresentation.iff_locallyOfFiniteType.mpr
    (locallyOfFiniteType_pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C))
```

The landed LFT theorem is [Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:433](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:433), quasi-compactness is [Pic0SepClosedJacobianData.lean:101](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedJacobianData.lean:101), and mathlib supplies LFT ⇒ LFP over a locally Noetherian base plus quasi-separatedness in `Noetherian.lean` lines 264 and 220.

Finally, [Pic0RepresentabilityDescentData.lean:412](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0RepresentabilityDescentData.lean:412) only packages overlap descent data after a representative over a fixed extension has been supplied. It neither descends the carrier nor proves effectiveness. Therefore Phase 7 still needs, independently:

1. Scheme-object spread of the qc finitely presented separable-closure representer.
2. Delta-colimit descent of the universal Pic0 element and equality witnesses.
3. Verification that the descended element represents the finite-stage functor, ultimately producing `Σ L, PicRepDatum k L.1 ((baseChange k L.1).obj C)`.
